description: Still trying to find our way
summary: MoonScope is a web app that answers one question for a lunar south pole landing: will this lander survive at this site, on this date? At the pole the Sun circles low along the horizon, so hills can hide the Sun (no solar power) and Earth (no radio contact) for days. Using real NASA data (LRO LOLA terrain and NAIF SPICE Sun and Earth positions), MoonScope simulates every hour of a mission at 9 candidate landing sites and shows when the lander will be in shadow or out of contact, and whether its battery survives. It then finds the smallest change that saves a failing plan: land a day later, move to another site, use a bigger battery or less power. It also checks whether a 1 km landing miss would end the mission. This helps mission planners and students choose safer landing sites and dates before touchdown, explained in simple words.
details:
Live app: https://moonscope-two.vercel.app/

Source code: https://github.com/NoshinSyaraPromitee/Team_Merge_Conflict_Nasa_Space_App_Challenge


WHAT IT DOES

MoonScope checks whether a lander at the Moon's south pole will survive its mission. You pick one of 9 landing sites (or type your own point near one) and a landing date, then set battery size, power use, solar panel efficiency, mission length and the hours of Earth contact needed per day. MoonScope simulates every hour and gives a clear result: FEASIBLE, AT RISK or INFEASIBLE.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Terrain: from the LOLA 20 m south pole height map (NASA PGDA product 90) we compute the horizon around each landing point and 24 nearby points (a 5 x 5 km grid).

2. Sun and Earth: NAIF SPICE kernels (DE440, Moon frames, leap seconds) give the Sun and Earth position in the sky every hour for a year.

3. Light and contact: if the Sun is above the local hills the panels charge; if Earth is above them the lander can talk to Earth (good, weak or lost).

4. Battery: an hour-by-hour energy model. The mission fails if the battery drops below 25% or Earth contact per day is too short.

5. Fixes: MoonScope re-runs the simulation to find the smallest change that saves a failing plan, and checks every suggestion before showing it.

SURVIVAL GUIDE (REAL PLANNING)

- Planner: 2D map or 3D Moon with real sunlight, the local sky, an hour-by-hour timeline, key numbers, the lander's 360-degree view of the hills, what-if tests, side-by-side comparison, recommended fixes, mission alerts, and "Ask MoonScope" (type a change in plain words).

- Landing accuracy check: re-runs the whole mission at 25 points within 2 km, because a lander can miss its target by about 1 km. "Try a landing" drops the lander with a random miss. At a peak like Malapert, 1 km off can mean no Sun or no Earth.

- Mission brief: a one-page report of the plan that can be printed or saved as a PDF.

- Survival Calendar: every landing date for the next 60 days, coloured by result, with the first date the mission fails.

- Shadow DNA: a light-and-contact fingerprint for every site, side by side.

GAME (PRACTICE)

- Rescue Mode: something goes wrong after landing (dust on the panels, a late landing, a stuck heater). Choose moves to keep the battery alive for 72 hours while our rover acts out every move.

HOW WE CHECKED IT

- Sun and Earth geometry checked against SPICE within 0.003 degrees.

- Sunlight compared with NASA's PGDA product 69 south pole illumination maps (method in docs/METHOD.md).

- 342 automated tests (205 for the web app, 137 for the Python pipeline and data).

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

A fast first check for mission planners, students and space fans: it finds dangerous shadows and radio blackouts before landing, shows how sensitive a plan is to delays and landing errors, and explains everything in simple words. A guided tour and plain-language guide make it usable by non-experts.

TOOLS

Web app: React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Zustand, Recharts, three.js (React Three Fiber), Motion, Rive, Vitest. Hosted on Vercel.

Data pipeline: Python, NumPy, spiceypy (SPICE), pyerfa, matplotlib, pytest.

Code: https://github.com/NoshinSyaraPromitee/Team_Merge_Conflict_Nasa_Space_App_Challenge
